title: Accurate Evaluation of Nanoscale Spatiotemporal Dynamics with Electron Correlation Microscopy
authors: Po-Cheng Kung, Ajay Annamareddy, Mark D. Ediger, Dane Morgan, Paul M. Voyles
abstract: Electron correlation microscopy (ECM) can measure materials dynamics with nanoscale spatial resolution from intensity correlation functions. However, adopting X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) normalization frameworks unchanged when calculating intensity correlations can introduce errors. Due to the constrained sampling volumes and larger speckle sizes in nanobeam electron diffraction, XPCS-style time-averaging and scattering-vector averaging introduce systematic artifacts, such as artificial anticorrelations or elevated baselines that lead to systematic errors in structural relaxation times and stretching exponents. This work presents physics-inspired, ECM-specific intensity normalizations over time- and azimuthal-averaged intensities of the first diffraction ring that limit those errors. The framework is validated using molecular dynamics simulations of a CuZr supercooled liquid to benchmark against the self intermediate scattering function, successfully reproducing relaxation times. When applied to experimental time-resolved 4D STEM datasets of a Pt57.5Cu14.7Ni5.3P22.5 nanowire, the method correctly identifies highly stable, unchanging nanoscale crystalline phases that were erroneously misclassified as relaxing domains by previous frameworks. Other previous ECM research is reevaluated in light of these observation. This robust approach establishes an artifact-free pathway for evaluating localized spatiotemporal relaxation behaviors.
summary: This paper addresses systematic errors in measuring nanoscale structural dynamics using Electron Correlation Microscopy by proposing a novel, physics-inspired intensity normalization technique. The method corrects for artifacts arising from misapplying X-ray scattering analysis tools (XPCS) to electron diffraction data. By validating this approach against simulations and applying it to experimental samples, the authors establish an artifact-free pathway for characterizing localized structural relaxation in disordered materials.
main_problem: Previous Electron Correlation Microscopy (ECM) methods incorrectly applied X-ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy (XPCS) normalization frameworks to nanobeam electron diffraction data, leading to systematic errors in measuring nanoscale structural relaxation times.
main_result: The authors developed a physics-inspired, ECM-specific normalization framework that successfully reproduces known relaxation dynamics using molecular dynamics simulations and correctly identifies stable crystalline phases in experimental nanowire data previously misclassified as relaxing domains.
method: They propose an alternative intensity normalization scheme based on time- and azimuthal-averaging of the first diffraction ring intensities, which corrects for artifacts inherent to conventional XPCS analysis in nanoscale electron scattering geometries.
model_or_system: The work uses molecular dynamics simulations of a supercooled liquid (CuZr) as a benchmark, and applies the method to experimental time-resolved 4D STEM datasets of a complex metallic nanowire ($	ext{Pt}_{57.5}	ext{Cu}_{14.7}	ext{Ni}_{5.3}	ext{P}_{22.5}$).
key_observables: Structural relaxation times and stretching exponents derived from intensity autocorrelation functions, specifically the self-intermediate scattering function ($	ext{self-ISF}$), $	ext{g}_2$, and $	ext{c}_2$.
important_parameters: Nanoscale spatial resolution (1 nm probe size); time delays ($\Delta t$); temperature/cooling rate regimes in supercooled liquids.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the systematic errors arise from inappropriate normalization; the proposed method assumes isotropy and uses specific averaging over diffraction rings to correct for these artifacts.
figures_summary: Figure 12 compares simulated X-ray and electron scattering normalized intensity profiles, highlighting the difference between standard XPCS ranges and the actual electron speckle diameter sampled by ECM.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the systematic failure of XPCS normalization in ECM; it then proposes a new physics-inspired normalization framework; this is validated using MD simulations of supercooled liquids ($	ext{CuZr}$); finally, the method is applied to analyze experimental 4D STEM data on nanowires.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial methodological rigor for interpreting complex scattering data from disordered systems (like glasses or amorphous materials), which is highly relevant to understanding structural relaxation dynamics in condensed matter theory and experiment.
